objective: Run the eighth B-52 refinement rung with the alternative pre-registered alongside the monotonicity prediction, and measure whether the recipe refines the near-body cells uniformly between rungs or merely rescales the background block, which is the mechanism that would explain seven non-monotone rungs
rationale: This is agp-1dec50b65c2f made launchable, with the one addition the record says it needs. The ladder in the B-52 uncertainty study record runs 0.05512, 0.04477, 0.04905, 0.04720, 0.04957, 0.05228, 0.04822 at 40,656 to 441,057 cells, monotone false, conclusive false, band recorded as the largest spread times 1.25 at 0.00507. Rung 7 was pre-registered with a prediction that Cd would rise and that prediction scored FALSE, which is on the record in the rung 7 results write-up. An eighth rung that predicts monotonicity again is making the same bet a second time and would learn nothing new from a second miss. The alternative that has never been measured is in the ladder's own notes: every rung from production onward scales the background blockMesh divisions (41x36x60, then 46x40x67, 51x45x75, 55x49x82) while holding the near-body shell level at 2 and the maximum cell level at 4. If the near-body refinement levels are fixed, the cells at the surface where the drag is integrated may barely move between rungs while the total cell count nearly doubles, and a ladder whose refinement does not reach the integration surface is not a uniform refinement and cannot produce an observed order however many rungs it gets. That is a measurement, not an opinion: it is the surface-cell size and the surface-cell count per rung, and it can be read off meshes that already exist before the eighth is generated.
gate: Two verdicts, both pre-registered before the rung is launched. First, zero compute, on the six meshes already on disk: the minimum and mean surface cell size on the aircraft patches per rung, and the count of surface faces per rung, against the total cell count per rung. If surface resolution is flat or near-flat while total cells nearly double, the ladder is not a uniform refinement and the non-monotonicity has a mechanism, which is reported as the primary result. Second, the eighth rung itself: Cd at roughly 880,000 cells on the same recipe, and the observed order recomputed through the lab's own Eca and Hoekstra band function with the conclusive flag recorded as it falls. A non-monotone eighth rung is a result and is reported as one
cost_basis: estimate, and its known weakness is restated rather than repaired. The finest rung holds 441,057 cells and the next roughly doubles it; rung 7 solved at 2 MPI ranks with 220,529 cells per rank. This figure prices the grid alone. The ladder stores cells per rung and no iterations, and measured cost rises about linearly with iterations while cells barely move within a family, so the iteration count is the term that can overrun and it is not priced here. The first half of this item costs 0 core-min because it reads meshes that already exist
expected_knowledge_gain: Either half pays and the cheap half pays first. If the surface-resolution measurement shows the recipe does not refine where the drag is integrated, seven rungs of non-monotone Cd are explained by a mechanism rather than left as a mystery, the conservative band stops being the only available answer, and every other ladder built on a scaled-background recipe inherits the same question, which is a transferable finding about our own method. If surface resolution does track the cell count, that hypothesis is refuted for the cost of reading six meshes and the eighth rung's number stands on its own as the settling evidence agp-1dec50b65c2f asked for

launch_prompt: B-52 eighth refinement rung. Read demo-output/website/campaign/NEXT_CASES_SLATE.md item 2, models/curriculum/uq-studies/b52.json and B52_RUNG7_PREREGISTRATION.md first. DO THE ZERO-COMPUTE HALF FIRST and write it down before generating any mesh: for each of the six existing rung meshes, report the aircraft-patch surface face count and the minimum and mean surface cell size against that rung's total cell count. The recipe scales the background blockMesh divisions while holding near_body_shell_level 2 and max_cell_level 4, so the hypothesis under test is that surface resolution is flat while total cells nearly double. If it is flat, that is the primary result and it explains seven non-monotone rungs; say so before the eighth rung's number exists, so the finding cannot be accused of following the answer. Then the rung: same recipe, system/ copied verbatim from study-b52-rung7-uq with only blockMeshDict changed, background divisions scaled again from 55x49x82 to roughly 880,000 cells, 2 MPI ranks, 300 iterations as every rung before it. Pre-register the Cd prediction AND the alternative before launching, and note in the pre-registration that rung 7's rise prediction scored FALSE so a second monotonicity prediction is a repeat bet. Recompute the observed order through the lab's own uq.eca_hoekstra_band and record the conclusive flag as it falls -- do not clamp it. Budget 20 core-min for the solve plus meshing, setsid, poll logs inline, and watch the iteration count: the cost basis prices the grid only and iterations are the term that overruns. Record: evidence file in demo-output/website/campaign/, docket update on agp-1dec50b65c2f and this item, honest verdict.
